channel.title: Maritime & Trade Wire (sample)
channel.description: Recorded sample feed used for offline development.

item.title: Antwerp-Bruges reports berth delays of up to 36 hours as strike spillover bites
item.description: Terminal operators at Antwerp-Bruges warn of a growing backlog after vessels diverted from Rotterdam. Average waiting time has risen sharply and yard density is above 85 per cent.

item.title: EU adopts new sanctions package restricting port calls for listed vessels
item.description: The new regulation bans port access across all member states for a further 44 listed vessels and tightens customs inspection requirements for transhipped cargo.

item.title: Low water on the Rhine forces barge operators to cut loadings
item.description: River levels at Kaub have fallen below 80 cm, restricting barge drafts. Operators are applying low-water surcharges and shifting volume to rail.

item.title: Ransomware attack disrupts terminal IT systems at Port Klang
item.description: A ransomware incident has taken gate and yard planning systems offline at one Port Klang terminal. Operations have moved to manual processing and truck turn times have doubled.

item.title: Interview: the terminal chief who says automation is oversold
item.description: A wide-ranging interview on labour, capital expenditure and why the industry keeps buying cranes it cannot staff.

item.title: Savannah terminals to shut ahead of hurricane landfall
item.description: The Georgia Ports Authority confirmed all Savannah container terminals will suspend operations from 1800 local, with cranes secured and gates closed to truck traffic.
